result.detailed_feedback:
**Element Layout (13.5 points):**
The split-screen design effectively balances textual definitions on the left with dynamic visuals on the right. Proper use of whitespace ensures the interface remains uncluttered during complex geometric transitions.

**Attractiveness (12.8 points):**
The minimalist dark theme provides excellent contrast for the neon-styled geometric lines. While professional and focused, the visual style is utilitarian and lacks decorative flair.

**Logic Flow (14.2 points):**
The pedagogical scaffolding is strong, progressing logically from basic dimensional building blocks to complex 4D concepts. The inclusion of the spider puzzle serves as an effective practical application of the theory.

**Accuracy & Depth (13.8 points):**
Content is mathematically sound, accurately depicting cube nets, cross-sections, and orthographic projections. It provides sufficient depth for an introductory understanding of dimensional shifts.

**Visual Consistency (13.2 points):**
The video maintains a cohesive aesthetic through consistent typography, line weights, and color-coded highlights. Transitions between static text and animated sequences are fluid and well-timed.

**Overall Summary:**
This video is a highly effective educational tool that uses clear animations to demystify abstract geometric concepts. Its strength lies in its logical progression and clear visual metaphors for dimensional changes.

**Key Strengths:**
• Clear pedagogical scaffolding
• High-contrast, readable visual design
• Effective use of the spider puzzle for practical application

**Areas for Improvement:**
• Incorporate more varied color palettes to distinguish dimensions
• Add brief interactive prompts or pauses for learner reflection

The volume of a cube is calculated by cubing its side length (V = s³). With a side length of 4, the volume is 4 * 4 * 4 = 64 cubic units.

C
A cube has six square faces. Slicing a cube with a plane parallel to one of its faces will result in a cross-section that is identical in shape and size to that face, which is a square.

The cookie cutter creates a 2D outline of a cat. Extruding this shape upwards adds a third dimension (height), thus transitioning the flat 2D shape into a 3D object.
